The standard Fréchet log integral reduces the ratio exactly to xi^(1-s) ∫z²/[z²+(1+xi)z+xi(1-t)]² dz, s=(1-α)/α. The scalar envelope xi^(1-s)/(1+xi) decays at both ends and is uniquely maximized at xi=(1-s)/s. A strictly positive integrand comparison yields continuous attained C_s(t), strict increase and strict subalignment deficit. Uniform near-zero resolvent expansion gives I_0-I_{xi δ}=(2xi/(1+xi)^3)δ log(1/δ)+O(δ) on compact xi; maximizers stay compact and converge to the scalar optimizer, so the exact cusp coefficient is 2s(1-s)s^s(1-s)^(1-s). No assertion at t=0 or α endpoints. Independent 30 quadrature/optimization corroborations supplement the uniform analytic proof.
